feature: The starter Button comes as Primary, Secondary or Ghost, in three sizes, with an icon
summary: The Button on the Library shelf now arrives the way the variants mock draws it: Primary, Secondary or Ghost in Small, Medium or Large, with a leading icon a copy can hide or swap for Wand, Swatch, Layers or Brush. A dropped copy starts as Primary, Medium.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default, in a new document. Walk: Scripts/playtest/starter-button-looks-walk.json.

try.do: Open the Library, drag Button onto the canvas and look at Properties: Variant, Size, then Show icon, Label and Icon.
Click Large under Size. The copy grows to 40 tall; press Command Z once to put it back.
Click Secondary, then Ghost, under Variant.
Click the Show icon switch. The icon goes and the button closes up round its word.
Press Command Z, open the Icon menu and pick Wand.
Click Large again. The Large button still leads with the wand.
Drag the button wider by a corner handle: the icon and word stay together in the middle.
Click the component field and choose Edit Original to see the nine looks in their grid.

evaluate: Does a dropped Button now look like a finished button you would ship, or still like a placeholder?
Is No icon at the foot of the Icon menu, turning the Show icon switch Off, the behaviour you expect, or should the two stay separate?
Do the Small, Medium and Large heights (24, 32, 40) feel right next to the rest of a screen you are building?
Is starting every copy on Primary, Medium the right default, or should a copy start on the top-left look of the grid?
rough: Primary is a flat accent blue where the mock draws a soft gloss and a lighter top edge; filed as the-starter-button-primary-shines-like-the-mock.
The Icon field shows only the icon's name where the mock shows the icon in front of it; filed as the-starter-button-primary-shines-like-the-mock. The menu rows do carry each icon's picture.
Secondary is a plain white surface with a hairline where the mock draws a glass control; it reads the same on a white canvas and is settled in the-starter-button-primary-shines-like-the-mock.

In dark mode the button keeps its light colours, where the mock also draws dark cells; that is decision card decide-whether-starter-components-change-colour-when-the-mac-is-in-dark-mode-sho, recommended to keep them.
Picking No icon turns Show icon Off rather than greying the switch as the mock does: the app goes further than the mock by making them one fact, so the switch always says what the canvas shows.

On Edit Original the nine looks are crowded: each drawing's name chip covers part of the Large column, and the Ghost row's grey words almost vanish on the page's dark backdrop; folded into edit-original-draws-a-two-question-component-ins and raised to p1.

The starter's accent and quiet text are now the design system's (#4C6FFF, #5C6371), so a Badge or Button dropped into a new document is a little bluer than before; documents that already took a starter keep theirs.
